Hey Samir — quick technical reply with what we can support out of the box and a couple implementation examples. TL;DR: yes, we can accept and propagate trace context, and we can emit token-level latency headers and structured logs you can pick up in your OTEL pipeline.

Supported telemetry and headers (we can customize names):
- Trace/context propagation: accepts W3C Trace-Context (traceparent) and a custom X-Redwood-Trace header. When traceparent is provided, Redwood will associate tokens/segments with that trace and emit spans to the console.
- Request ID: X-Redwood-Request-Id (UUID) — echoed back in our logs and response headers.
- Latency breakdown headers: X-Redwood-Latency-Total-ms, X-Redwood-Latency-Model-ms, X-Redwood-Latency-Embed-ms, X-Redwood-Latency-Rerank-ms. These are emitted on the response for sync calls; for streaming calls we include periodic progress headers and final totals.
- Routing: header-based routing supported via X-Redwood-Region (e.g., us-west-2) or X-Redwood-Pool (customer-pool-id). We can also accept SNI routing for TLS if you prefer.
- Structured output / tool calling: when using function/tool-calling, we emit a structured JSON field in logs: redwood.tool_call = {"name":"<tool>","args":{...},"duration_ms":123}. We will make sure the SDK includes an example of binding these to your OTEL resource attributes.

Example Node SDK snippet (API key auth, propagate incoming traceparent):

const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });

async function callModel(req, res) {
  const traceparent = req.headers['traceparent'] || req.headers['x-redwood-trace'];
  const headers = { 'traceparent': traceparent, 'x-redwood-region': 'us-west-2', 'x-redwood-request-id': generateUuid() };
  const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-llama-3', prompt: '...', headers });
  // server logs will include: trace_id, request_id, model, tokens_generated, latency_ms, breakdowns
  res.json(resp.body);
}

We recommend you map our response headers into your aggregation rules in Tempo/Prometheus: capture X-Redwood-Request-Id and the latency headers as attributes on spans. We can provide a Filebeat / OTLP config snippet to forward logs that include the redwood.* fields.

Attachments: example-trace-span.json (sample __otlp__ span payload), redwood-sdk-observability-guide.pdf (checklist).

Open question for FinTechCo: does your security team want API keys rotated via your KMS, or would you prefer we enable mTLS with customer certificates for the private endpoint? Either is fine; mTLS gives stronger assurance but adds ops work on your side.
